# Context-Rich Solid Mechanics Problem

## Bending Stress in a Cantilevered Industrial Operator-Seat Support

### Engineering Context

An industrial machine uses a side-mounted operator seat so that a technician can remain near a control or inspection station without placing a support column beneath the seat. The seat is carried by a hollow rectangular steel-tube arm projecting from the machine frame. The seat and occupant produce a downward load at an offset from the frame, creating shear and bending in the arm.

The structural review focuses on whether the selected tube geometry produces an acceptable bending stress at a designated section near the machine attachment. Local weld and bolt stresses, fatigue, impact, and dynamic seat loads are outside the base problem.

![Cantilevered industrial operator seat attached to a machine frame by a hollow rectangular support arm.](assets/seat-industry-context.png){fig-alt="Side-mounted industrial operator seat supported by a cantilever arm attached to a machine frame." width=88%}

### Main Engineering Goal

Determine the maximum normal bending stress at section a-a of the hollow rectangular support arm, identify the extreme fibers in tension and compression, and explain how the design could be modified to reduce bending demand.

### System Components

- operator seat and occupant load;
- vertical seat post and mounting bracket;
- hollow rectangular steel-tube cantilever arm;
- fixed machine-frame attachment at A; and
- machine frame carrying the reactions.
